item.title: BUILDING SERVICES FEES TO INCREASE JANUARY 22, 2026
item.description:
NOTICE

BUILDING SERVICES FEES TO INCREASE

Effective Thursday, January 22, 2026, Building Services fees will increase. The new fees are calculated using the 2025 Combined Development Related Fee Schedule.  

Some of the revisions in the 2025 Combined Development Related Fee Schedule include:

  • 1, 2, and 3 Family Dwelling Building Permit Fees
    • Alterations/Accessory Structures with 2 inspections
      • $385.00
    • Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing with 2 inspections
      • $275.00
    • Minor Work Permit with 1 inspection
      • $140.00
    • Deck
      • $375.00
  • Commercial/Mixed Use and Multi-Family Building Permit Fees
    • New Construction, Additions, Alterations and Accessory Structures including Swimming Pools with 2 inspections
      • $700.00 for the first 1,000 square feet
      • $7.00 for each 10 gross square feet or portion thereof after the initial 1,000 square feet
    • Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing with 2 inspections
      • $550.00 with 1 inspection
      • $700.00 with 2 inspection
    • Minor Work Permit with 1 inspection
      • $275.00
  • Miscellaneous Fees
    • Additional Inspection Trip
      • $225.00
    • Commercial and Multi-Family Plan Revisions, Plan Review and Preliminary Plan Review
      • $500. 00 for first hour
      • $225.00 for additional hour
    • After Hours Plan Review 
      • $2200.00
      • $225.00 each additional hour after

To view and download the new fee schedule visit https://www.columbus.gov/Business-Development/Building-Zoning-Services/Documents-Forms

Final Fee Schedule - https://www.columbus.gov/files/sharedassets/city/v/1/building-and-zoning/2026-fee-schedule-final.pdf

Red Lined - https://www.columbus.gov/files/sharedassets/city/v/1/building-and-zoning/2026-fee-schedule-red-line-final.pdf

If you have any questions, please send an email to:  BZSRecords@columbus.gov

item.title: Building Permit Application Revised
item.description:
August 11, 2025

NOTICE:  Building Permit Application revised

The Department of Building and Zoning Services revised the Building Permit Application to delete outdated information and provide more detailed information for our customers.  The Building Permit Application is completed and submitted with paper plans to Building and Zoning Services for review. All BZS applications are available in the Documents and Forms section of our website columbus.gov/bzs. Completion of the Building Permit Application is not required if applying for permits through the Citizen Access Portal.

Effective Tuesday September 2nd, 2025, previous versions of the Building Permit Application will no longer be accepted.

Please note that most permits can be applied for through the Citizen Access Portal.  Visit portal.columbus.gov for all online services.

###

item.title: SECURITY CHANGES AT COLEMAN GOVERNMENT BUILDING
item.description:
SECURITY CHANGES AT COLEMAN GOVERNMENT BUILDING

Beginning March 31, 2025, visitors will be required to check-in at 111 N. Front Street.  A new security desk is now located at the main entry on the north side of the building. Here's what to expect upon entering the building:

  • Visitors will be greeted by a security specialist. You will be asked for a valid ID and the specialist will begin the check-in process.
  • Once completed, you will receive a visitor sticker badge that must be worn at all times while in the building.
  • You will then proceed to the x-ray machine to place any belongings to be scanned and proceed through the metal detector.  At this point you will be free to drop off or collect approved plans at the BZS counter, as you do now. 

 The security desk will be occupied during the normal business hours of the building.

 

###

item.title: PHISHING EMAIL FROM BZS-PLEASE DELETE
item.description:
PHISHING EMAIL NOTICE:

2025 Combined Development Related Fee Schedule ref::#5606

Please delete the above titled email requesting review of documents from a Building and Zoning Services employee, as it is fraudulent.

In an effort to curb these types of mails, contact your email provider as they may use an email verification technology known as DMARC. This allows recipients of such emails to be able to tell if it is an official email from a real Columbus.gov email account or not. You will need to turn on DMARC verification with your email provider to take advantage of the technology. This should allow your email security filtering software to automatically reject such malicious messages claiming to be from the city.

We apologize for any inconvenience.

 

###

item.title: Citizen Access Portal and automated inspection line RESTORED
item.description:
CITIZEN’S ACCESS PORTAL & AUTOMATED INSPECTION LINE RESTORED

The Department of Building and Zoning Services is pleased to share that our Citizen Access Portal and automated inspection scheduling line, 614-645-8235, have been restored.  The portal can once again be used to schedule inspections, purchase inspection trips, submit permits, site engineering, and zoning letter applications, among other uses. The YouTube playlist linked below provides tutorial videos to certain aspects of using Citizens Access.

https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLDzGbueVklj0Y9FxFlpeP3WJpbO8cvMh

Thank you for your patience during the outage, and as we work to catch up on the emails, messages and paper applications we received over the past couple of weeks.

###

item.title: Building and Zoning Services is now responsible for private water and fire service inspections for underground lines
item.description:
Building and Zoning Services is now responsible for private water and fire service inspections for underground lines

The Department of Building and Zoning Services is now responsible for private water and fire service inspections for underground lines between the meter and/or after the backflow preventer and the structure based on the WSP.  Additional questions may be directed to the plumbing inspection section at plumbinginfo@columbus.gov.

To schedule an inspection you will first need to follow these steps to purchase a water service record through the Citizen Access Portal.

  • Create an account and log in, then associate your City of Columbus registration number to your account.
  • Under building, click purchase permit or inspection trip.
  • Select the appropriate registration and follow the steps to create a water service record.
  • After the record is paid for and issued inspections can be scheduled through Citizen Access or the automated inspection scheduling line for Building and Zoning Services.
  • Similar to other Building and Zoning Services permits the water service records are issued with a set number of inspection trips.
    • Each time an inspector visits the site a trip is debited from the record.
    • When the balance of trips available is zero a trip will need to be purchased before an inspection can be scheduled.

The YouTube playlist linked below provides tutorial videos on some aspects of Citizen Access including how to create an account, associate a registration to an account, and schedule an inspection.

https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLDzGbueVklj0Y9uFxFlpeP3WJpbO8cvMh
